Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

expose verb

to danger, harm, the weather

also exposed, expose oneself to, put at risk, leave exposed, unprotected

classical

Cic. Off. 1.83: nē offerāmus nōs perīculīs sine causā (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 7.77: sē mortī

offerō, offerre, obtulī, oblātum

irregular verb, with the dative: sē perīculīs offerre

expose (oneself) to

Of exposing oneself, willingly, to danger or death. Its everyday sense is to offer or present.

Other words

  • objiciō, objicere, objēcī, objectum — expose, put in the way of

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 37 (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.C. 1.64.4: exercitum … flūminī

    To throw or put something in front of someone or something, and so to expose to danger. It also means to throw something to someone (food to a dog: Verg. A. 6.421) and to reproach someone with something (objicere alicui aliquid).

  • nūdō, nūdāre, nūdāvī, nūdātum — leave exposed, undefended

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 2.6: mūrus dēfēnsōribus nūdātus (Lewis & Short)

    Properly to strip or bare; in war, to leave a place without defenders.

Examples

  • nē offerāmus nōs perīculīs sine causā

    let us not expose ourselves to danger without good reasonCic. Off. 1.83 (Lewis & Short)

See also expose, risk, protect, uncover.

SourcesLewis & Short: offero · Lewis & Short: obicio · Lewis & Short: nudo
